title: Measuring Validator and Sandboxed-Execution Coverage for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts: A Paired Confirmatory Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) to quantify the marginal detection benefit of adding automated sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator for LLM-generated intent→configuration artifacts. Using shared_initial_candidate semantics and the declared model "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses), we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks drawn from a deterministic synthetic task bank. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. The paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Model-call accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These results fall far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20); we report the preregistered design, exact artifact-grounded outcomes, a clarified explanation of provider-call audit fields, an artifact-grounded interpretation of the negligible guarded benefit in this regime, and concise pointers to the archived execution manifest for independent verification.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Operational deployment requires generated artifacts to satisfy syntactic correctness, workflow ordering, and higher‑order safety constraints. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute, sometimes augmented by sandboxed emulation to reveal runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and system reports document this pattern and argue for workflow-centred evaluation, but they provide limited large-scale paired measures of the marginal value added by sandboxed execution [1]–[3].

Research question and contributions. Preregistered question: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and faithful autonomous execution on Npairs = 720; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis with exact counts and inferential outcomes; (3) a clarified methods description that reconciles provider-call accounting with pair accounting under shared_initial_candidate semantics; (4) an evidence-grounded interpretation of the observed near-zero marginal guarded benefit and concrete boundary conditions where guarded stages will likely matter.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centred mitigations and verification tools. Recent surveys and architecture reports document practical trendlines for pairing LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to raise operational assurance for NetOps artifacts [1]. Tool and prototype studies show that static validators catch many classes of errors (syntactic, simple workflow constraints, and many invariants), while emulation can expose runtime-dependent behaviors and stateful interactions that static rules miss [2], [3].

Empirical positioning. Prior empirical work in adjacent domains (program/spec verification and LLM-assisted synthesis) shows that generate→validate→repair approaches improve correctness but that marginal gains from runtime execution depend strongly on task distribution, validator coverage, and emulator fidelity [1], [2]. These findings motivated our paired design under shared_initial_candidate semantics to isolate only downstream guarded-stage effects (emulation or repair) and not generation variability.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Planned Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440); minimum effect-of-interest for power planning = 0.20. Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds. Missingness and contamination rules, multiplicity handling for exploratory tests, and deterministic reconciliation procedures were fixed in the preregistration.

Task bank and shared_initial_candidate enforcement. Confirmatory items were produced deterministically from an intent_configuration_repair_v1 generator covering three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates (leaf–spine, 3-node service chain, triangle). For each pair we obtained exactly one sampled initial candidate (a single provider call) and that identical candidate was presented to both downstream pipelines (baseline and guarded). This isolates guarded-stage effects by removing generation sampling variability as a discordance source.

Validator and emulator implementations. Baseline: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 — a rules-based validator performing vendor-CLI parsing, command canonicalization, sequence-order checks against required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break), protected-interface invariants, group-activity constraints, and final-state conformance. Guarded pipeline: runs the baseline validator and then executes the candidate in a sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices; the harness records runtime observations (interface transitions, transient concurrent-interface states, MTU/VLAN application effects, topology-level reachability) and maps those observations to runtime-observation rules that can trigger guarded detection if they reveal violations not encoded by the static validator.

Provider-call audit fields and reconciliation (clarification requested by reviewers). The archived execution manifest records per-run provider-call auditing. Important audit fields and their artifact-grounded meanings in this run are: (a) hosted_model_call_event_count = 721: the total number of hosted-model calls issued; (b) stage_counts: {shared_initial_generation: 720, repair: 1} — counts of calls attributed to logical protocol stages; (c) condition_counts: {"shared": 720, "guarded": 1} — counts of model calls that the orchestration recorded as associated with the shared initial generation stage (the single sampled candidate reused across both conditions) versus additional guarded-stage model calls (repairs) executed only for the guarded pipeline. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics, the single shared_initial_generation call per pair is reused by both conditions; thus condition_counts may appear asymmetric while pair accounting remains symmetric because the shared call is not duplicated. Deterministic reconciliation confirms complete_pair_count = 720, completed_episode_count = 1440, and stage_counts and condition_counts map to the single documented repair-stage invocation (repair = 1) plus the 720 shared initial calls. These artifact-grounded audit entries explain why a condition-level call-count asymmetry does not imply unequal pair-level sample sizes: the majority of model calls were the single shared initial generation reused across both conditions, while the single extra call was a repair-stage invocation performed only in the guarded pipeline. The manifest and reconciliation artifacts provide the trace linking the unique guarded-only detection to that single repair-stage call.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory counts and inferential outputs (artifact-grounded). Analysis artifacts report contingency counts: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 721 (shared_initial_generation = 720; repair = 1). Complete_pair_count = 720 and failed_episode_count = 0 under the preregistered missingness policy.

Discordant-pair attribution. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, any discordant guarded-only detection must originate from either (i) an emulation-observed runtime violation not present in the static validator rules, or (ii) a guarded-stage repair invocation that altered the candidate. Provider-call audit and deterministic reconciliation show a single repair-stage call (repair = 1) that corresponds to the unique n10 discordant record. The archived raw_results.jsonl contains the per-episode traces (validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields) needed to locate that pair_id and to inspect whether the guarded-only detection arose from emulation observation or from the repair. We do not reproduce logs here; the execution manifest is the canonical artifact pointer for auditors.
sections.discussion:
Why was the guarded-stage aggregate benefit negligible? The artifact-grounded evidence supports three factors.

Validator ceiling effect. The deterministic validator explicitly encoded the workflow constraints exercised by the curated tasks (patterns such as shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break_uplink_switchover, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). Representative validator_traces show parsed_command_count equal to required_command_count and violation_count = 0 for most pairs; baseline success rate = 719/720 indicates almost complete validator coverage in this constrained bank, leaving little room for emulation to add detections.

Curated, parser-validated tasks. Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance, which removed many malformed or adversarial candidates. The confirmatory bank therefore underrepresents task regimes where runtime-only faults typically appear; deterministic_reconciliation reports zero irrecoverable parser exclusions, confirming a tightly curated set.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity. By design the identical sampled candidate served both conditions. Provider-call auditing shows only one additional guarded-stage repair call across the entire run; that single extra call maps to the single observed guarded-only detection. Thus the observed aggregate marginal gain is narrowly localized to one downstream event rather than to a systematic emulation advantage across the bank.

Operational implications. For operator workflows that enforce parser validation and employ a high-coverage static validator tailored to expected intent patterns, adding automated sandboxed emulation may yield negligible incremental detection benefit at scale. However, this conclusion is conditional: in noisier, adversarial, or more diverse vendor/CLI regimes, or with higher-fidelity emulation of long-lived control-plane dynamics, guarded stages can surface failures that static validators cannot capture. Our archived artifacts provide concrete seed cases for adversarial extension work.
sections.conclusion:
We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows one repair-stage invocation corresponding to the single guarded-only detection; shared_initial_candidate semantics ensure discordance sources are downstream. We interpret this narrow near-zero finding as arising from validator ceiling effects and the curated task design. Future work should retest guarded stages under adversarial tasks, expanded vendor diversity, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where sandboxing provides substantive operational value.

Reproducibility note. The execution manifest and archived bundle are the canonical reproducibility artifacts for independent auditors; they contain per-episode raw_results, reconciliation artifacts linking provider-call audit to episode traces, and the analysis artifacts that produced the numeric outputs reported above (see Disclosure for the canonical manifest pointer).

limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in the archived execution manifest and reconciliation artifacts.
